quality._variant_perception_note: Every BUY must state the market's misunderstanding explicitly: what consensus believes, what the agent believes differently, the specific mispriced mechanism, and the event/date when the market finds out. Enforced as a required BUY field; format documented in CLAUDE.md.
quality._risk_map_scenarios_note: risk_map and scenarios were always in the CLAUDE.md schema but not validator-enforced, so proposals omitted scenarios and the published scenario_ev stayed empty. Now required on every BUY.
quality._thesis_invalidators_note: Binding falsifiers (not vibes): object with invalidating_print, invalidating_structure, time_box — each a non-empty string. Enforced on every BUY so re-underwrites have kill criteria.
quality._demand_driver_note: Primary demand-driver theme for theme concentration (e.g. hyperscaler_server_capex, ai_compute_gpu). Distinct from GICS sector. See tools/demand_drivers.py and context bundle demand_driver_map.
quality._required_sell_fields_note: SELL_TO_CLOSE needs only these; the BUY-oriented required_proposal_fields list used to reject legitimate discretionary exits for missing stop_loss/target_price. Prefer also exit_reason when available (process, not hard-required).
quality._volatility_stop_note: A stop tighter than the name's noise is not protection - it exits on ordinary volatility, not on a broken thesis. The stop must sit at least max(min_stop_atr_multiple x 14d-ATR%, min_stop_expected_move_fraction x options expected_move%) below entry. Enforced only when volatility data is present (fail-open). If that floor exceeds max_stop_loss_distance_pct, the name is too volatile for a valid swing stop and is rejected.

original_plan.thesis: Dell is the best risk/reward in an extended AI-server complex: it pairs elite momentum (+143% 3m, +202% 6m) with the cheapest valuation in the group (forward P/E ~20.9, P/S 2.2) and a constructive entry, having pulled back only 2.2% from its 20-day high while sitting 4.1% off its 52-week high near a buy point. The 29% collapse in Super Micro is a direct tailwind, consolidating enterprise/AI-server share toward Dell as customers de-risk suppliers. Q1 fundamentals (revenue $23.4B, net income $965M) confirm profitable scale, and the current tape ('Dell Stock Nears Buy Point') shows institutional demand building. With no earnings until 9/3, a 45-day swing captures the momentum leg without event risk.
catalysts: Breakout through the buy point on sustained AI-server order momentum over the next 2-4 weeks
Continued Super Micro share-shift narrative benefiting Dell (ongoing, July 2026)
Positive pre-announcement/analyst upgrades ahead of the Sept 3 earnings print
original_plan.risk_map: The trade breaks if AI-server demand cools or gross-margin fears (the Super Micro overhang) spread to Dell - watched via any negative pre-announcement, channel checks, or a close back below the 50-DMA. A broader chip/AI momentum unwind driven by the rising-rate/sticky-inflation backdrop would also hit it; the 408 stop (-9.4% from last close, within ATR) caps the loss and exits before the thesis fully unwinds.
original_plan.macro_context: Regime is supportive for AI/data-center longs: falling Fed funds, tight credit spreads, low VIX (16.9) and easy financial conditions, with the tape confirming a chip/AI-led Nasdaq rally. The one caveat is re-accelerating CPI (4.27%) and rising long rates (10Y 4.56%), which pressure the highest-multiple names most - precisely why Dell's ~21x forward multiple is the right way to express this trade rather than a 40-100x momentum name.

original_plan.thesis: HPE is the most valuation-protected way to own the AI-server/networking buildout in a tape where reaccelerating inflation (CPI 4.27%) and a rising 10-year (4.56%) are punishing rich multiples. It trades at just ~12.2x forward earnings and 1.67x sales - the cheapest in the server group - after a record fiscal Q2 and the completed Juniper acquisition, which adds a scaled networking franchise. Sell-side has responded with a +40.5% 30-day upward EPS revision, yet the stock is consolidating (1m +1.4%) and sits 23.8% below its 52-week high, so estimates are rising while price has not re-rated. The same SMCI collapse (-29%) that helps Dell consolidates enterprise AI-server demand toward HPE as customers de-risk suppliers. With the last print already behind it (38 days ago) and no earnings inside the 40-day window, this is a clean cheap-re-rating swing.
catalysts: Juniper integration/synergy updates and combined AI-networking order commentary over the coming weeks
Continued upward analyst EPS revisions re-rating a 12x multiple toward peers (multiple 'undervalued' calls this week)
Enterprise AI-server share consolidation following the SMCI -29% collapse
original_plan.risk_map: The trade dies if the Juniper integration disappoints or the record Q2 proves a peak (the quarter carried a -$1.05B Juniper-related charge), or if a cheap-but-thin-momentum name simply goes dead money with no near-term dated catalyst. Early warnings: a break below the 50-DMA / the $43.75 stop, EPS revisions rolling over from up to down, or server-group leadership (DELL) breaking down in sympathy. Because this adds a second servers_hardware name alongside DELL (~18% combined, well under the 40% cap), a sector-wide AI-capex scare would hit both - I'd cut faster if the group leader cracks.
original_plan.macro_context: The regime is net supportive - tight HY spreads (2.70), low VIX (15.84), loosening financial conditions (NFCI -0.52) - which favors staying long the AI/data-center complex. But CPI has reaccelerated to 4.27% and the 10-year has risen to 4.56%, a combination that compresses the highest multiples. HPE is deliberately chosen as the valuation-protected expression of that view: at ~12x forward with rising estimates, it carries far less multiple-compression risk than the 40x+ momentum leaders if yields keep climbing.

position_histories.note: Last 10 daily sessions for each CURRENT HOLDING, newest last, with 5-day change and distance from the 10-day high/low. Use this to judge whether a position is resting, breaking down, or extended - not just today's print vs the entry plan.

position_stop_cushion.note: For each open position: room left between today's price and your recorded stop, measured in the name's own ATR. cushion_in_atr < 1 (inside_noise_band true) means one ordinary session could hit the stop - decide deliberately (hold through it, or exit on your terms) rather than get noise-stopped. The safety layer still enforces the recorded stop on a closing basis.

stop_engineering.note: ENFORCED stop floor per name. Your stop_loss must sit at least min_stop_distance_pct below entry or the validator rejects it (stop_inside_noise_band). This is a floor, not a target - for a swing hold, aim WIDER (roughly 1.5-2x ATR, or clearly beyond the expected move) so ordinary volatility does not stop you out. If tradeable is false the name is too volatile for a valid stop under the 15% cap; do not propose it.

recent.note: Weekly self-review: This week was mostly build week, not trade week - the system went from a bare skeleton to a full pipeline (data relay, validator, position sizing, watchlist triggers, insider activity, sector relative strength, post-earnings drift detection) in a handful of commits, and only opened its first two live paper positions on 7/9 (DELL) and 7/10 (HPE). Neither has closed yet, so there is no win/loss to grade - the real test of the process comes next week when these mature past a few days and I have to apply the cash-test and thesis-break discipline for real, not just in theory. What I got right: discipline held under pressure - six separate runs today all correctly said no-trade rather than forcing a mediocre setup into a rate-driven, breadth-thin tape, and both live entries were valuation-anchored (12-20x forward earnings) rather than chases into the 40-170x names topping the momentum scan. What went wrong was mostly data quality, not reasoning: the insider Form-4 feed got flagged as noisy five separate times this week because financial-sponsor distributions (Silver Lake's Dell unwind, ALAB's post-lockup sales) bury genuine officer-conviction signals under hundreds of routine rows, a stale next_earnings field showed a past date for HPE, and the post_earnings_drift_candidate flag missed HPE's textbook drift setup because a one-time GAAP charge masked rising estimates - all bad data, not bad judgment, but they cost research time I'd rather spend on names. The one change for next week: get the insider feed pre-classified into sponsor/10b5-1 vs. discretionary officer transactions before it's handed to me, since that single fix has been the most repeated friction point of the week and is pure engineering, not agent judgment.

process_checklist.note: Required reasoning order every run. Work top-down; do not propose a BUY before completing the steps above it. Cite the relevant context-bundle blocks in commentary when a step changes your aggression.

steps.title: Macro regime check
steps.must: Read macro_regime (+ market_events / market_news tape). State whether the regime supports adding long swing exposure. Hostile or rolling leadership -> raise the bar, prefer cash / exits.

steps.title: Portfolio / book review
steps.must: Re-underwrite every open position with fresh research: HOLD or SELL_TO_CLOSE. Thesis broken = exit. Cash test: if remaining expected return no longer clearly beats cash yield, rotate. Honor stops, stall flags, and forced-exit aftermath.

steps.title: Idea selection
steps.must: From universe_scan / watchlist / tape promotions, pick at most a handful of candidates. Prefer fat pitches over marginal RR. Empty proposals with a clear no_trade_reason is a valid outcome.

steps.title: Entry geometry & underwrite
steps.must: For each candidate: charts, volume, stop/target geometry, fundamentals freshness, filings, catalysts. WebSearch mandatory before proposing a BUY. Variant perception required. Size and RR must clear validator floors as a MINIMUM, not a target.

steps.title: Kill conditions
steps.must: State what kills the trade and how you would know early (risk_map). Pre-plan stop, horizon, and invalidation before size. If kill conditions are fuzzy, do not buy — watchlist it.

reasoning_process.full_run_no_trade_rule: On full depth with empty proposals, include rejected_ideas: [{ticker, reason}, ...] with at least 2 scan ideas you passed on.

price_freshness.note: Prefer universe_scan.prices_meta[T].price_as_of (bar session date) over bundle age alone. On catalyst days, verify live before chasing a trigger on a lagging close.

reasoning_process.demand_driver_map_note: Primary economic bet per ticker (not GICS). Use these labels in proposal.demand_driver. Theme cap is separate from sector cap.

learning_pack.note: LEARNING PACK (top 5 each). Full histories live in state/ archive and data/*.json — do not need them unless drilling. Use this pack for decisions: regrets, good skips, binding exits, left-on-table with WHY, adopted lessons, calibration phase.

hold_winners_playbook.when_left_on_table_repeats: Use sell_fraction (e.g. 0.4–0.6) to bank, trail rest with structure (raise stop under higher lows / 50-DMA) while invalidators clear.
hold_winners_playbook.when_why_is_catalyst: Leftover gains were news/event-driven after exit — before full exits, check earnings/catalyst calendar; prefer partials into known events.
hold_winners_playbook.when_why_is_technical: Leftover gains were trend continuation without a clear new catalyst — if structure + invalidators still clear, trail instead of full close.
hold_winners_playbook.when_good_lock_in_repeats: Full exits into strength then fade are fine — do not force trails when leadership is rolling over.
hold_winners_playbook.never: Never ignore stops or invalidators just to 'let it run' — that is hope. Running winners means planned partials, not deleting risk.

steps.must: State what kills the trade and how you would know early (risk_map). Pre-plan stop, horizon, and invalidation before size. If kill conditions are fuzzy, do not buy — watchlist it.

watchlist_feedback.note: Watchlist foresight / opportunity-cost feedback. hits_not_bought = names still on the watchlist whose stated buy level was reached but you never bought. opportunity_cost = large moves (or hit-then-dropped) without action — grade whether the pass was discipline or a miss. Do NOT chase a name just because it moved; use this to sharpen when you write would_buy_at and when you act on triggers.

hits_not_bought.why: buy level hit while still on watchlist — not bought

hits_not_bought.one_line: Networking backbone for AI clusters, fair valuation, one price tick from our stated buy trigger.

price_freshness.note: Prefer universe_scan.prices_meta[T].price_as_of (bar session date) over bundle age alone. On catalyst days, verify live before chasing a trigger on a lagging close.
